mainTopic: Setting שביתה at a distance, the source and shape of the 2,000-אמה תחום, and the poor man's עירוב with his feet
overview: The amud opens with רבא's condition: a traveler may set his שביתה at a distant tree only if he could reach it by running before Shabbat. אביי objects from the משנה's words 'it got dark on him,' and the גמרא explains that this means only that he can no longer reach his house. In a story, רבה sets a שביתה for himself and רב יוסף under a famous palm tree that רב יוסף does not know. רבה supports this with רבי יוסי's ברייתא, though the גמרא says he used רבי יוסי's name mainly so that רב יוסף would accept the ruling. The גמרא then asks where the 2,000-אמה תחום comes from. רב חסדא answers with a chain of גזירה שוה links ending at the ערי הלוים, and the גמרא defends it against a challenge from the 1,000-אמה פסוק. Next comes a dispute over whether the תחום is a circle (רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס) or a square (רבנן, from רב חנניה's 'כזה'), and the square idea is applied to carrying ארבע אמות and to a pillar's width. Finally the משנה about a poor person making an עירוב with his feet is quoted. רב נחמן begins explaining the מחלוקת, and his explanation continues on the next amud.

steps.title: רבא: he must be able to reach the tree by running
steps.stepSummary: רבא limits the משנה's rule: declaring שביתה at the tree's base works only if, by running, he could reach it before Shabbat.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: This rule applies only when, if he ran to the base of the tree, he would get there before Shabbat.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא adds a condition to the משנה about the traveler who names a tree as his Shabbat 'home.' The tree must be close enough to reach by running before Shabbat starts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה lets a traveler set his שביתה at a tree he sees in the distance. רבא says this cannot be any tree at all. It must be within reach, at least by running, before nightfall.

keyTerms.meaning: 'and that is only when'; introduces a limiting condition

steps.whyThisMatters: It sets the limit on how far away a declared שביתה can be: the place must be reachable before Shabbat.

phrases.english: Rava said:
And that is only when, if he would run to its base, he would arrive (before Shabbat).
phrases.notes: This adds a limit to what the משנה said.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Comments on the משנה (49b) about a traveler who declares his שביתה at a tree.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Declaring שביתה at a tree's base is valid only if he could reach it by running before Shabbat.

steps.title: אביי: the משנה says 'it got dark on him'
steps.stepSummary: אביי challenges רבא: the משנה describes the person as already overtaken by darkness, so how can he still reach the tree?
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: But the משנה says 'it got dark on him'!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי challenges רבא's condition using the משנה's own words.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'It got dark on him' sounds like it is too late to reach anywhere. If so, the משנה cannot be talking only about someone who can still reach the tree, and רבא's condition seems to contradict the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: it got dark on him (night overtook him)
'but it teaches...'; an objection from the wording of a source

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:
But it teaches 'it got dark on him'!
phrases.notes: These are the משנה's own words.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רבא's condition from step 1.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's condition that he can reach the tree before Shabbat.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה's phrase 'it got dark on him' implies he can no longer reach anywhere before nightfall.

steps.title: Dark only relative to his house
steps.stepSummary: 'It got dark' means he can no longer reach his home, but he can still reach the tree.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'It got dark' means it is too late for him to reach his house. But he can still get to the base of the tree.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers אביי by explaining what 'it got dark on him' really means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Darkness here is measured against his house, which is far away. The tree is closer, so he can still reach it. The משנה's wording and רבא's condition fit together.
steps.confusionAlert: 'It got dark' does not mean Shabbat has already started. It means he is too late to get home, while closer places can still be reached.

phrases.english: 'It got dark' with respect to his house,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל לְעִיקָּרוֹ שֶׁל אִילָן מָצֵי אָזֵיל.
phrases.english: but to the base of the tree he is able to go.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אביי's challenge in step 2.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'It got dark on him' means he cannot reach any place before Shabbat.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'It got dark' refers only to reaching his house. The nearer tree is still reachable.

steps.title: Second version: dark only if walking slowly
steps.stepSummary: In another version, רבא himself explains 'it got dark' as referring to slow walking. If he runs, he arrives.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say רבא said: 'It got dark on him' means if he walked slowly. But if he runs, he gets there.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a different version of רבא's statement. Here רבא builds the explanation of 'it got dark' right into his reading of the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this version there is no back-and-forth with אביי. רבא reads 'it got dark' as 'too late if he walks slowly,' while running still gets him there in time. The practical result matches the first version: the place must be reachable by running.
steps.whatToRemember: Both versions agree: the declared spot must be reachable before Shabbat at least by running. 'It got dark' does not mean it is impossible to arrive.

phrases.english: Some say Rava said:

phrases.aramaic: חָשְׁכָה לוֹ כִּי מְסַגֵּי קַלִּי קַלִּי,
phrases.english: 'It got dark on him' when he walks slowly,
but if he runs, he arrives.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: An alternate transmission of רבא's statement from steps 1 to 3.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'It got dark' means too late at a slow walk. If running gets him there, the שביתה is valid.

steps.title: רבה names a famous palm tree as their residence
steps.stepSummary: While traveling with רב יוסף, רבה declares their שביתה under a well-known palm tree, described in two versions.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה and רב יוסף were traveling on the road. רבה said to רב יוסף: 'Our שביתה will be under the palm tree that carries its brother.' Some say he said: 'under the palm tree that saved its owner from the land tax.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a real-life story that applies the law of declaring שביתה at a tree. This story sets up the next question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה names one שביתה for both of them, using a famous landmark tree. The two versions just describe the tree differently: one leaning on another palm, or one so productive it paid its owner's whole tax.

keyTerms.meaning: that carries its brother (another palm leans on it)

phrases.aramaic: רַבָּה וְרַב יוֹסֵף הֲווֹ קָא אָזְלִי בְּאוֹרְחָא.
phrases.english: Rabba and Rav Yosef were going along the way.
Rabba said to Rav Yosef:
Let our residence be beneath the palm tree
that carries its brother.
And some say:
beneath the palm tree that redeemed its owner from the land tax.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבָּה וְרַב יוֹסֵף הֲווֹ קָא אָזְלִי בְּאוֹרְחָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the משנה's law to a story that applies it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבה declares a joint שביתה beneath a known palm tree.

steps.title: רבה asks if רב יוסף knows the tree
steps.stepSummary: רבה asks whether רב יוסף recognizes the tree. רב יוסף says he does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Does the Master know it?' He said to him: 'I do not know it.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבה checks whether רב יוסף recognizes the tree. This matters because you can only set שביתה at a place you know. The answer sets up רבה's next move.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A traveler can name a landmark as his שביתה only if he recognizes it. רב יוסף does not know this palm, so on his own he could not use it, and a solution is needed.

phrases.english: Does the master know it?
He said to him: I do not know it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows up on רבה's declaration in step 5.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether רב יוסף recognizes the named tree.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רב יוסף does not recognize it.

steps.title: Rely on me: רבי יוסי's ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: רבה tells רב יוסף to rely on him, citing רבי יוסי: someone who does not recognize a place may hand his שביתה to a companion who does.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: 'Rely on me.' As the ברייתא teaches: רבי יוסי says, if there were two people, one who recognizes the place and one who does not, the one who does not recognize it hands his שביתה over to the one who does. The one who recognizes it says, 'Our שביתה is in such-and-such place.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבה solves the problem with a ברייתא. רב יוסף can let רבה, who knows the tree, set the שביתה for both of them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Not knowing the tree would normally stop רב יוסף from using it. רבי יוסי allows him to entrust his שביתה to someone who knows the place, and the knower's declaration covers both. This is exactly the source for what רבה did.
steps.whatToRemember: A person who does not recognize a landmark can still set his שביתה there by entrusting it to a companion who does recognize it (רבי יוסי).
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that setting a שביתה can be done on someone's behalf when he hands it over.

phrases.english: He said to him: Rely on me,
as it was taught: Rabbi Yosei says:
If there were two people,
one who recognizes (the place) and one who does not recognize it,

phrases.aramaic: זֶה שֶׁאֵינוֹ מַכִּיר מוֹסֵר שְׁבִיתָתוֹ לַמַּכִּיר,
phrases.english: the one who does not recognize it hands over his residence to the one who recognizes it,
and the one who recognizes it says:
'Let our residence be in such-and-such place.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the problem raised in step 6 with a ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: רבה's ability to declare a שביתה for רב יוסף at a tree רב יוסף does not know.
steps.raayaSupportSource: ברייתא of רבי יוסי: the non-recognizer hands his שביתה to the recognizer.

steps.title: רבה only used רבי יוסי's name so רב יוסף would accept the ruling
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says the ruling is not just רבי יוסי's individual view. רבה used רבי יוסי's name only because רב יוסף would accept a ruling from someone known for solid reasoning.
steps.simpleTranslation: But it is not so. רבה did not really teach it to him as a view held only by רבי יוסי. He did it so that רב יוסף would accept it from him, because רבי יוסי's reasoning is always with him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא steps in and says that the ruling רבה gave in step 7 is not only רבי יוסי's opinion. רבה attached that name as a persuasion tool.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 7, רבה supported his ruling by quoting רבי יוסי. Here the גמרא says the ruling does not depend on רבי יוסי alone. רבה chose רבי יוסי's name because רבי יוסי is known as 'נימוקו עמו', meaning his rulings rest on sound reasoning, so רב יוסף would not argue.

keyTerms.meaning: But it is not so (the גמרא rejects what was just said)
His reasoning is with him, meaning his rulings are well-founded

steps.confusionAlert: This does not mean רבה's ruling was wrong. The גמרא only says that the ruling is not only רבי יוסי's view. רבה named רבי יוסי to persuade רב יוסף.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that the name a teacher attaches to a ruling can carry weight. Citing a rabbi whose rulings are known to be well-reasoned makes the listener more ready to accept the ruling.

phrases.english: But it is not so;
he did not teach it to him as Rabbi Yosei's view
phrases.notes: רבה did not truly cite it because it was רבי יוסי's ruling.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא כִּי הֵיכִי דְּלִיקַבֵּל לַהּ מִינֵּיהּ,
phrases.english: except so that he would accept it from him,
because Rabbi Yosei's reasoning is with him.
phrases.notes: רבי יוסי is known for well-reasoned rulings.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלָא הִיא, לָא תְּנָא לֵיהּ כְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the idea that the ruling in step 7 is held only by רבי יוסי.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the attribution of the ruling to רבי יוסי, not the ruling itself.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רבה's citation was not meant to mark this as רבי יוסי's view specifically. He named רבי יוסי to persuade רב יוסף, because רבי יוסי's reasoning is well-founded.

steps.title: Back to the משנה: someone who does not know a landmark
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה about a person who does not recognize a landmark or does not know the הלכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'If he does not recognize, or is not an expert, and so on.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a new line from the משנה. This sets up the next discussion: that such a person gets 2,000 אמה from where he stands.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה teaches that someone who cannot set his שביתה at a distant landmark acquires it right where he stands. From there he may walk 2,000 אמה in every direction. That number is what the גמרא will now examine.

phrases.english: If he does not recognize
or if he is not an expert, etc.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִם אֵינוֹ מַכִּיר אוֹ שֶׁאֵינוֹ בָּקִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves away from the story of רבה and רב יוסף to a new line of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One who cannot set שביתה at a landmark acquires 2,000 אמה from where he stands.

steps.title: Where does the Torah write the 2,000 cubits?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the Torah source of the 2,000-אמה limit.
steps.simpleTranslation: These 2,000 אמה, where are they written?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a basic question: where in the Torah does the 2,000-אמה limit come from?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה treats 2,000 אמה as obvious. The גמרא wants to find where this measure comes from in the Torah.

phrases.english: These two thousand cubits,
where are they written?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the number mentioned in the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The Torah source for the 2,000-אמה תחום.

steps.title: A ברייתא reads the 4 and 2,000 cubits into the verse
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא reads 'שבו איש תחתיו' as 4 אמות and 'אל יצא איש ממקומו' as 2,000 אמה.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא taught: 'Stay, every man, in his place' means 4 אמות. 'Let no man go out of his place' means 2,000 אמה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a ברייתא that finds both measures in one פסוק about the מן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'תחתיו' (in his spot) means the small 4-אמה area. 'ממקומו' (from his place) means the full 2,000 אמה. But the ברייתא does not show why 'place' should equal 2,000. That gap sets up the next question.

keyTerms.meaning: Stay, every man, in his spot (שמות טז:כט)
Four cubits, the smallest personal space

phrases.english: As it was taught: "Remain every man in his place"
these are four cubits.
"Let no man go out of his place"
these are two thousand cubits.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 10.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The word 'ממקומו' in שמות טז:כט is the source for 2,000 אמה.

steps.title: How do we know 'place' means 2,000 cubits?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how we know that the word 'מקום' means exactly 2,000 אמה.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do we know this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא presses further: the פסוק only says 'his place', so where does the number 2,000 come from?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא connected 'מקום' to 2,000 אמה but gave no source for the number. The גמרא now asks for a source that defines 'מקום' as 2,000.

phrases.english: From where do we derive it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the basis behind the ברייתא's reading.

steps.title: רב חסדא's chain of word links leading to 2,000 cubits
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא links 'מקום' through a chain of גזירה שוה words (place, fleeing, border, outside) to the פסוק that measures 2,000 אמה outside the ערי הלוים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: We learn 'place' from 'place', 'place' from 'fleeing', 'fleeing' from 'fleeing', 'fleeing' from 'border', 'border' from 'border', 'border' from 'outside', and 'outside' from 'outside'. As it is written: 'And you shall measure from outside the city, on the east side, 2,000 cubits.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא answers with a chain of matching words. The chain carries the meaning of 'מקום' all the way to a פסוק that says '2,000 cubits'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'מקום' at the מן links to 'מקום' by the עיר מקלט, where 'נסה' (fleeing) also appears. From there, each link uses two words that share a פסוק: fleeing goes to border, and border goes to outside. The last link reaches 'מחוץ' in the פסוק of the ערי הלוים, which states 2,000 אמה. That number then travels back to 'מקום' at שבת.
steps.whatToRemember: The 2,000-אמה תחום comes from 'ממקומו'. Its number is found through a chain of word links that ends at the 2,000 אמה around the ערי הלוים.
steps.confusionAlert: Each link is not a separate rule. Picture a chain: the same word joins two פסוקים, and a second word in the same פסוק carries the meaning to the next link.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the Torah basis given for the 2,000-אמה תחום שבת that the whole מסכת relies on.

phrases.english: Rav Chisda said:
We derive "place" from "place,"
phrases.notes: The word 'place' about Shabbat is linked to 'place' said about the accidental killer (שמות כא:יג).

phrases.english: and "place" from "fleeing,"
and "fleeing" from "fleeing,"
phrases.notes: This links to במדבר לה:כו.

phrases.english: and "fleeing" from "border,"
and "border" from "border,"
phrases.notes: This links to במדבר לה:כז.

phrases.english: and "border" from "outside,"
and "outside" from "outside."
As it is written: "And you shall measure from outside the city
phrases.notes: This is the פסוק of the ערי הלוים (במדבר לה:ה).

phrases.english: on the east side
two thousand cubits, etc."

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא: לָמַדְנוּ מָקוֹם מִמָּקוֹם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 12 by giving the source for 'מקום' meaning 2,000 אמה.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A chain of גזירה שוה links connects 'מקום' to the 2,000 אמה measured outside the ערי הלוים.

steps.title: Why not learn from the 1,000-אמה פסוק?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב חסדא's chain: the word 'וחוצה' in the 1,000-אמה פסוק could serve as the link instead.
steps.simpleTranslation: But let us learn instead from the פסוק 'from the wall of the city outward, a thousand אמה'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the last link in רב חסדא's chain. Two neighboring פסוקים about the ערי הלוים both use an 'outside' word. One gives 1,000 אמה and the other gives 2,000 אמה. So why pick the 2,000?
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב חסדא linked 'חוץ' to the פסוק that measures 2,000 אמה outside the city. But just one פסוק earlier (במדבר ל״ה:ד׳), the Torah says 'וחוצה אלף אמה', which is 1,000 אמה outside the wall. If we linked to that פסוק instead, the תחום שבת would be only 1,000 אמה.

keyTerms.meaning: But let us learn (derive) instead from

steps.confusionAlert: Both numbers come from the same section about the ערי הלוים: 1,000 אמה in one פסוק and 2,000 אמה in the next. The גמרא is asking which of the two the 'חוץ' link should connect to.

phrases.english: But let us derive from 'the wall of the city'
phrases.notes: Quoting במדבר ל״ה:ד׳

phrases.english: 'outward, a thousand cubits'?
phrases.notes: This would give a limit of only 1,000 אמה

steps.triggerLanguage: וְנֵילַף מִ״קִּיר הָעִיר וָחוּצָה אֶלֶף אַמָּה״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges which פסוק the final link of רב חסדא's גזירה שוה chain should connect to
steps.kashyaTarget: רב חסדא's choice of the 2,000-אמה פסוק as the end of the chain
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A neighboring פסוק also has an 'outside' word but says 1,000 אמה, so the link could just as easily point there.

steps.title: Link 'חוץ' only to the identical word 'חוץ'
steps.stepSummary: We learn 'חוץ' from the identical word 'חוץ', not from the slightly different word 'חוצה'.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learn 'חוץ' from 'חוץ', but we do not learn 'חוץ' from 'חוצה'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that a גזירה שוה connects matching words. The 2,000-אמה פסוק says 'מחוץ', which matches exactly. The 1,000-אמה פסוק says 'וחוצה', which is a slightly different form of the word.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word in the עיר מקלט פסוק is 'חוץ'. The 2,000-אמה פסוק also says 'חוץ' ('מחוץ לעיר'), so it is an exact match. 'חוצה' has an extra letter, so it is not the same word, and the 1,000-אמה option is rejected.

keyTerms.meaning: We derive (learn one case from another)

phrases.english: We derive 'outside' from 'outside',
phrases.notes: It's the exact same word in both places.

phrases.english: but we do not derive 'outside' from 'outward'.
phrases.notes: An extra letter makes it a different word

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 14
steps.terutzResolutionType: Exact wording: a גזירה שוה requires identical words
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any 'outside' word, including 'וחוצה', could serve as the link
steps.terutzMaskana: Only the identical word 'חוץ' links, so the limit is 2,000 אמה

steps.title: Even different words are linked elsewhere
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that the school of רבי ישמעאל links even two different words ('ושב' and 'ובא'), so one letter should not matter.
steps.simpleTranslation: What difference does it make? The school of רבי ישמעאל taught: 'And the כהן shall return' and 'And the כהן shall come': returning and coming are treated as the same!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer it just gave. If a גזירה שוה can link two totally different words, then a one-letter difference like 'חוץ' and 'חוצה' should certainly not stop it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the laws of נגעי בתים, the פסוק of 'returning' (שיבה) states the timing: 'ושב הכהן ביום השביעי', on the seventh day. The school of רבי ישמעאל applies that same timing to the כהן's 'coming' (ביאה), even though שב and בא are different words. This shows that a גזירה שוה does not always require identical words, so the answer in step 15 seems too strict.

keyTerms.meaning: And what difference does it make?
It was taught in the school of רבי ישמעאל

phrases.english: And what difference does it make?
phrases.notes: He's asking why it should matter whether it says 'חוץ' or 'חוצה'.

phrases.english: But the school of Rabbi Yishmael taught:
'And the priest shall return,' 'and the priest shall come':
phrases.notes: ויקרא י״ד:ל״ט and י״ד:מ״ד, about נגעי בתים

phrases.aramaic: זוֹ הִיא שִׁיבָה, זוֹ הִיא בִּיאָה!
phrases.english: this is returning, and this is coming (they are the same)!
phrases.notes: Even though the words are different, they're still linked.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמַאי נָפְקָא מִינַּהּ? הָא תָּנָא דְּבֵי רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer given in step 15
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that a גזירה שוה requires identical words
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If entirely different words (שב/בא) can be linked, a one-letter difference (חוץ/חוצה) surely should not block the link.

steps.title: Use the exact match when one exists
steps.stepSummary: Linking non-identical words is allowed only when no identical word is available. When an exact match exists, we use it.
steps.simpleTranslation: That applies only where there is nothing exactly like it. But where there is something exactly like it, we learn from the thing that is exactly like it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the objection. The school of רבי ישמעאל linked different words only because no exact match was available. Here an exact 'חוץ' does exist, so we must use it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two approaches do not contradict each other. Similar words can be linked only as a fallback. Since the 2,000-אמה פסוק has the exact word 'חוץ', it takes priority over 'חוצה', and the limit remains 2,000 אמה.
steps.whatToRemember: The 2,000-אמה תחום comes from an exact 'חוץ'/'חוץ' match. A near match like 'חוצה' is used only when no exact match exists.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets a rule of priority for גזירה שוה: an identical word always beats a merely similar one.

phrases.english: This applies only where
phrases.notes: This puts a limit on the method of the school of רבי ישמעאל.

phrases.english: there is nothing identical to it,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל הֵיכָא דְּאִיכָּא מִידֵּי דְּדָמֵי לֵיהּ —
phrases.english: but where there is something identical to it,
we derive from what is identical to it.
phrases.notes: So 'חוץ' links to 'חוץ'

steps.triggerLanguage: הָנֵי מִילֵּי הֵיכָא דְּלֵיכָּא מִידֵּי דְּדָמֵי לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 16 and defends step 15
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the scope of the school of רבי ישמעאל's method
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since similar words can be linked, 'חוצה' is just as good as 'חוץ'
steps.terutzMaskana: An identical word takes priority, so 'חוץ' links to 'חוץ' and the limit is 2,000 אמה

steps.title: The משנה says 2,000 אמה in a circle
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next phrase of the משנה: the 2,000 אמה are measured as a circle.
steps.simpleTranslation: Two thousand אמה, measured in a circle.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves on to the next line of the משנה. In the משנה, רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס says the 2,000 אמה are measured as a circle, while the חכמים say they are measured as a square. This step sets up the question that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A circle means 2,000 אמה in every direction, measured evenly all around. A square, by contrast, also gives the extra space in the corners. The גמרא quotes this phrase so it can question the circle view.

phrases.english: Two thousand cubits, round.
phrases.notes: The view of רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס in the משנה

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to a new line of the משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס, the 2,000 אמה of the תחום are measured as a circle

steps.title: A two-sided challenge to the circle view
steps.stepSummary: Either way, רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס has a problem. If he accepts the גזירה שוה, the פסוק says 'sides', meaning a square. If he rejects it, he has no source for 2,000 אמה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס, whichever way you look at it: if he accepts the גזירה שוה, 'sides' is written in the פסוק. If he does not accept the גזירה שוה, where does he get 2,000 אמה from?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא traps רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס with a 'whichever way you look at it' question. Both possible positions seem to lead to trouble for him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 2,000 אמה come from the ערי הלוים פסוק through the גזירה שוה. That same פסוק speaks of 'פאת' (sides: east side, south side, and so on), which describes a square, not a circle. So if he uses the פסוק, he should hold square. If he does not use it, he loses the source for the number 2,000 entirely.

keyTerms.meaning: Whichever way you look at it (a two-sided challenge)
A link between two פסוקים through a shared word
Where does he get it from?

steps.confusionAlert: The same פסוק supplies both the number (2,000) and the shape (sides, meaning square). The trap is that רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס seems to want the number without the shape.

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבִּי חֲנִינָא בֶּן אַנְטִיגְנוֹס מָה נַפְשָׁךְ:
phrases.english: And Rabbi Ḥanina ben Antigenos, whichever way you look at it:
if he accepts the verbal analogy,
'sides' are written,
phrases.notes: במדבר ל״ה:ה׳ says 'פאת קדמה' and so on, which describes a square

phrases.english: if he does not accept the verbal analogy,
from where does he derive two thousand cubits?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי חֲנִינָא בֶּן אַנְטִיגְנוֹס מָה נַפְשָׁךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the circle view quoted in step 18, using the source from step 13
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס's view that the תחום is circular
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The only source for 2,000 אמה is the ערי הלוים פסוק, and that פסוק describes square 'sides'. Accepting the source forces a square, and rejecting it leaves no source for 2,000 at all.

steps.title: The word 'זה' limits square measuring to the ערי הלוים
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס does accept the גזירה שוה. The word 'זה' teaches that only the ערי הלוים get square corners, while people resting on Shabbat get a circle.
steps.simpleTranslation: Really, he does hold of the גזירה שוה. But here it is different, because the פסוק says: 'This shall be for them the open land of the cities.' To this, the open land of the cities, you give corners. You do not give corners to people resting on Shabbat.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from Step 19. רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס gets the 2,000 אמה from the גזירה שוה, but he does not take the square shape along with it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גזירה שוה teaches the distance of 2,000 אמה. The extra word 'זה' ('this') limits the square shape (פאות, corners) to the ערי הלוים only. So for Shabbat, he keeps the number but measures it as a circle.

keyTerms.meaning: Really / actually (introduces an answer that keeps the original position)
The open land around the cities of the Levites
People resting on Shabbat (measuring their תחום)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think he rejects the גזירה שוה. He uses it for the number 2,000. He only blocks the square shape from carrying over.

phrases.english: Really, he does hold of the verbal analogy,
but here it is different,
because the verse says:
'This shall be for them the open land of the cities' —
to this you give corners,
phrases.notes: The word 'זה', 'this', is read as a limit.

phrases.aramaic: וְאִי אַתָּה נוֹתֵן פֵּיאוֹת לְשׁוֹבְתֵי שַׁבָּת.
phrases.english: but you do not give corners to those resting on Shabbat.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְעוֹלָם אִית לֵיהּ גְּזֵירָה שָׁוָה, וְשָׁאנֵי הָכָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the 'either way' question from Step 19.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: If he accepts the גזירה שוה, it seems he must also accept the square shape.
steps.terutzMaskana: The גזירה שוה gives the 2,000 אמה. 'זה' limits the square shape to the ערי הלוים, so Shabbat measuring is a circle.

steps.title: How do the רבנן read the word 'זה'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the רבנן, who measure square, do with the word 'זה'.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the רבנן? (What do they learn from the word 'this'?)
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a short question that sets up the next step. If the רבנן measure Shabbat as a square, how do they explain the word 'זה'?
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס used 'זה' to exclude Shabbat from the square shape. The רבנן hold that Shabbat is square, so they must read 'זה' in some other way.

keyTerms.meaning: And the Rabbis? (what do they do with this source?)

phrases.english: And the Rabbis?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס's reading to the רבנן.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How the רבנן understand the word 'זה' in the פסוק.

steps.title: רב חנניה: all Shabbat measures are like this
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן read 'זה' as 'כזה', meaning all Shabbat measurements should be square like the ערי הלוים.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught in a ברייתא: רב חנניה says: Like this shall be all who rest on Shabbat.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a ברייתא. רב חנניה reads the word 'זה' to include Shabbat in the square shape.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same word gets the opposite reading. For רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס, 'זה' means 'only this' and excludes Shabbat. For the רבנן, it means 'like this' and makes the ערי הלוים the model for every Shabbat measure, so Shabbat is square too.
steps.whyThisMatters: רב חנניה's rule that all Shabbat measures are square is used again in Step 25 for a new question about a pillar.

phrases.english: It was taught: Rav Chananya says:
Like this shall be all who rest on Shabbat.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנֵי, רַב חֲנַנְיָה אוֹמֵר: כָּזֶה יְהוּ כׇּל שׁוֹבְתֵי שַׁבָּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 21.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The רבנן read 'זה' as 'כזה': all Shabbat measures are square like the ערי הלוים.

steps.title: Carrying ארבע אמות is measured including the diagonal
steps.stepSummary: רבי אחא בר יעקב says a person is only חייב for carrying four אמות in רשות הרבים if he carries the full length of the square's diagonal.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אחא בר יעקב said: One who carries four אמות in רשות הרבים is not חייב until he carries the length of the sides and their diagonal.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new statement that builds on the idea that Shabbat measures are square. Four אמות is treated as a square, and you must carry the length of its diagonal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If four אמות is a square, the longest distance across it is the diagonal, about 5.6 אמות. רבי אחא בר יעקב says a person is only חייב after carrying that full diagonal length, in any direction. Carrying just four straight אמות is not enough.

keyTerms.meaning: One who carries (an object across a distance)
Four אמות, the distance that makes one חייב for carrying

phrases.english: Rabbi Acha bar Yaakov said:
One who carries four cubits in the public domain
is not liable
until he carries them with their diagonal.
phrases.notes: The diagonal of a 4x4 square, about 5.6 אמות.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the square model of Shabbat measures to carrying four אמות.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A person is חייב for carrying in רשות הרבים only after carrying the full diagonal length of a 4x4 אמה square.

steps.title: רבא's test: does a pillar need the diagonal?
steps.stepSummary: רבא asked his students whether a pillar in רשות הרבים, ten טפחים high and four טפחים wide, needs a width of four including the diagonal.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: רבא tested us: A pillar in רשות הרבים that is ten טפחים high and four טפחים wide, does it need the sides and their diagonal, or not?
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא tells about a test question that רבא asked his students. Does the 'four טפחים' width of a pillar also follow the 'sides and diagonal' idea?
steps.deeperAnalysis: A pillar ten טפחים high and four טפחים wide counts as a רשות היחיד. רבא asks whether the four טפחים width must be a true square, with room for the diagonal. A plain width of four in one direction may not be enough.

keyTerms.meaning: Ten טפחים high and four טפחים wide, the size of a רשות היחיד

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא בָּדֵיק לַן רָבָא:
phrases.english: Rav Pappa said: Rava tested us:
A pillar in the public domain
ten handbreadths high and four wide,
does it need them with their diagonal, or not?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא בָּדֵיק לַן רָבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the 'sides and diagonal' idea from Step 23 to the width of a pillar.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a pillar's four טפחים width must include the diagonal of a square.

steps.title: The students answer from רב חנניה
steps.stepSummary: The students answered that this is exactly רב חנניה's teaching: all Shabbat measures are square, so the pillar needs a full four-by-four square.
steps.simpleTranslation: And we said to him: Isn't this the teaching of רב חנניה? As it was taught: רב חנניה says: Like this shall be all who rest on Shabbat.
steps.whatsHappening: The students answer רבא's test by quoting רב חנניה's ברייתא from Step 22. The answer is yes: the pillar must hold a full square.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since all Shabbat measures are square 'like this,' a pillar's four טפחים must be a real 4x4 square. If the pillar is not square-shaped, its width must reach the length of that square's diagonal. The same ברייתא that answered the רבנן's reading of 'זה' now answers a practical question.
steps.whatToRemember: רבנן: Shabbat measures are square ('כזה', like the ערי הלוים). רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס: a circle ('זה', only the ערי הלוים get corners). Because the measures are square, the diagonal counts, both for carrying four אמות and for a pillar's four טפחים.

phrases.english: And we said to him:
Is this not the teaching of Rav Chananya?
As it was taught: Rav Chananya says:
Like this shall be all who rest on Shabbat.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמְרִינַן לֵיהּ: לָאו הַיְינוּ דְּרַב חֲנַנְיָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבא's test from Step 24 using רב חנניה's ברייתא from Step 22.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Yes. Since all Shabbat measures are square, the pillar must hold a full 4x4 square, including the diagonal.

steps.title: The משנה: a poor person makes an עירוב with his feet
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה. A poor person can make an עירוב by walking, and רבי מאיר says only a poor person gets this leniency.
steps.simpleTranslation: And this is what the Sages meant when they said: a poor person makes an עירוב with his feet. רבי מאיר said: We only allow this for a poor person, etc.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves back to the משנה and quotes its next line. It sets up a new discussion about who is allowed to make an עירוב by walking instead of with bread.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally an עירוב תחומין is made by placing bread at a spot, which then counts as your Shabbat home. The משנה says a poor person, who may not have spare bread, can instead go to the spot himself and declare it his home. רבי מאיר limits this leniency to a poor person. The 'וכו׳' cuts off רבי יהודה's view in the משנה, which allows it for rich and poor alike.

keyTerms.meaning: An arrangement that sets a new 'home base' for Shabbat, so a person can walk 2000 אמות from there
A poor person, here someone without spare food for an עירוב
Makes the עירוב 'with his feet', by being physically present at the spot rather than placing bread there
'Etc.', meaning the quote continues in the משנה (here, רבי יהודה's opposing view)

steps.confusionAlert: The 'וכו׳' hides an important part of the משנה. רבי יהודה disagrees and says that both rich and poor can make an עירוב with their feet. You need his view to follow רב נחמן's explanation in the next step.

phrases.english: And this is what they [the Sages] said:
The poor person makes an eruv with his feet.
phrases.notes: He walks to the spot and declares it his Shabbat residence, without placing bread there.

phrases.english: Rabbi Meir said:

phrases.aramaic: אָנוּ אֵין לָנוּ אֶלָּא עָנִי וְכוּ׳.
phrases.english: We have [this leniency] only for a poor person, etc.
phrases.notes: The rest of the משנה: רבי יהודה says it applies to both poor and rich.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְזֶה הוּא שֶׁאָמְרוּ הֶעָנִי מְעָרֵב בְּרַגְלָיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the discussion of the 2,000-אמה תחום and its shape (steps 9–25) and returns to the next clause of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A poor person may establish an עירוב תחומין by his physical presence. According to רבי מאיר, this leniency is limited to a poor person.

steps.title: רב נחמן: the dispute is about saying 'my place', since רבי מאיר holds an עירוב is mainly bread
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן says רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה argue about a person who declares 'my residence is where I stand'. He begins with רבי מאיר's reason: the main form of עירוב is bread.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said: The disagreement is in a case where the person said 'in my place'. For רבי מאיר holds that the main way to make an עירוב is with bread...
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן defines the exact case of the מחלוקת in the משנה and starts explaining רבי מאיר's reasoning. The explanation of רבי יהודה's side continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב נחמן narrows the argument to someone who declares 'my Shabbat home is right here where I stand' (במקומי). רבי מאיר says bread is the real, primary עירוב. Walking with your feet is only a fallback for someone who has no bread, so a rich person cannot use it. The sentence is not finished, and רבי יהודה's opposing reason comes next.

keyTerms.meaning: A disagreement, here the one between רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה
'In my place', a declaration that one's Shabbat residence is right where one is standing
The primary, main form of the עירוב enactment
Bread, the standard item used to establish an עירוב

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the key idea of the sugya. The argument is really about which method is the 'main' עירוב, bread or feet. That decides whether walking is a full option for everyone or only a backup for the poor.

phrases.english: Rav Nachman said:
The dispute is [in a case where he said] 'in my place',
phrases.notes: He declared his residence to be the spot where he is standing.

phrases.english: for Rabbi Meir holds:
the primary [method of] eruv is with bread,
phrases.notes: So walking is only a fallback for a poor person. רבי יהודה's view continues on the next amud.

steps.alternativePossibleLabel: תשובה (implicitly defining the case of the משנה)
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the scope of the משנה's מחלוקת quoted in step 26 and gives the reasoning behind רבי מאיר's limitation.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The מחלוקת is about someone who declared 'במקומי'. רבי מאיר limits the foot-עירוב to the poor because he holds the primary עירוב is with bread.
